acceptance_test_matrix: Tumbling event-time windows assign events to exactly one fixed interval and emit exactly once when watermark passes the window end.
Sliding event-time windows assign one event to all expected overlapping windows and close each eligible window deterministically by watermark.
Processing-time tumbling and sliding windows trigger from deterministic runtime clock or timer advancement.
Late arrivals before bounded allow-lateness expiry update the target window only under allow-lateness policy.
Late arrivals beyond allowed-lateness expiry are dropped or rejected according to policy and do not reopen evicted windows.
Per-partition state isolation prevents aggregation across partitions with identical keys and window bounds.
Watermark advancement without additional input closes all eligible event-time windows in deterministic order and never closes future windows early.
Window state eviction removes closed stale windows after trigger emission and lateness expiry.
Invariant failure coverage asserts invalid window sizes, invalid slide durations, impossible lateness settings, and stale or invalid timestamps are rejected or contained without corrupting state.
Partial/failure acceptance covers no duplicate emissions after repeated watermark or timer advancement.
Benchmark smoke coverage includes the window node and jmhSmokeCheck is green.
Configured QA gate coverage includes qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, unit tests, and jmhSmokeCheck.
assumptions: Window API types belong in dag-framework-api/src/main/ while executable runtime node behavior belongs in runtime-core/src/main/.
Existing WatermarkPolicy and GraphPartitionRunner watermark/timer behavior are the integration points for event-time closure.
Processing-time windows can use existing deterministic runtime clock/timer primitives without wall-clock dependencies.
Benchmark validation is satisfied by extending the existing benchmark smoke surface rather than adding a new benchmark module layout.
Session windows, user-defined custom windows, and cross-partition window merging are explicitly out of scope.
